page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.24xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by custom AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors. It features 96 dedicated physical cores (96 vCPUs) running at 3.3 GHz with no hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For high-speed local storage, the instance is equipped with 5700 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Network connectivity is supported by a 50 Gbps baseline bandwidth, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the m9gd.24xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 191709.22 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 31014.0. Its memory subsystem delivers exceptional throughput, with read-only small block bandwidth reaching 13843.78 GB/sec and large block read bandwidth at 365.15 GB/sec. Single-core performance is moderate to strong, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2006.19. The server excels in database operations, recording a Passmark database score of 57407.22 and handling 268.05 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. It also shows strong capabilities in medium-sized LLM inference tasks, processing 232.81 tokens per second for 7B model prompts.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture combined with high-density local NVMe storage provides a highly resource-dense profile, offering significant compute and storage capacity without the overhead of external network-attached storage. The lack of hyperthreading ensures predictable, dedicated core performance. This server is highly suited for data-intensive workloads, including large-scale database hosting, Redis caching layers, high-throughput static web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale machine learning inference.
